MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 22, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 7:04 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045
Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of the Palos Verdes 4H Club led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager, Douglas R. Prichard
  City Attorney, Donald M. Davis
  Assistant City Manager, Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION FOR FIRE RESCUE (taken out of order – see below)

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
  Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to
  the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted one correction to be made on Item 5I, the Environmental
  Advisory Committee Minutes, indicating that on page two the motion should reflect the
  recommendation for 36% for NON-RESIDENTIAL customers.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-J AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JANUARY 22, 2019
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF DECEMBER 11, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF DECEMBER 11, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – DECEMBER 2018 AND JANUARY 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60987 THROUGH 61024 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $311,460.12 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 120118 THROUGH 120718;
  60811 THROUGH 60817; 60818 AND 60819 (VOID-PRINTER TESTING); 60850
  THROUGH 60862; 60863 (VOID-PRINTER TESTING); 60864 THROUGH 60868
  (VOID); 60869 THROUGH 60934 IN THE AMOUNT OF $470,820.02 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $782,280.14 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

E.  NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 3, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 17, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 15, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

J.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Dan Armendariz, District Manager, Cal Water provided an update on the status of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 22, 2019
 Recognizing that it was not yet 7:30 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL took New Business Item A out of
order.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH SOUTHWEST PIPELINE FOR “YEAR 1” STORM
  DRAIN PIPE REHABILITATION PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) authorize staff to amend the contract with
  Southwest Pipeline for the “Year 1” Storm Drain Pipe Rehabilitation Project for additional
  work in the amount of $88,425 and 2) allocate a contingency in the amount of $50,000 to
  address any additional unforeseen issues related to the storm drain repairs for this
  project.

  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the reason the costs for this project
  are exceeding the allocated contingency is due to the complicated nature of this type of
  project and because the pipes cannot be easily visually inspected. He also commented
  that this project is necessary for the safety of the community.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF regarding the flooding on Palos Verdes Drive
  East that occurred during the recent rains, Assistant City Manager Grammer commented
  that the flooding is due to storm drain related issues and that staff is assessing the
  situation to determine the best way to proceed. He explained the interim steps staff has
  taken to address public safety.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE STAFF TO AMEND THE CONTRACT
  WITH SOUTHWEST PIPELINE FOR THE “YEAR 1” STORM DRAIN PIPE
  REHABILITATION PROJECT FOR ADDITIONAL WORK IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $88,425 AND ALLOCATE A CONTINGENCY IN THE AMOUNT OF $50,000 TO
  ADDRESS ANY ADDITIONAL UNFORESEEN ISSUES RELATED TO THE
  STORM DRAIN REPAIRS FOR THIS PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

Recognizing that it was still not yet 7:30 p.m. and that a representative from Cal Water was
present, MAYOR MITCHELL took New Business Item C out of order.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 22, 2019
 C.  CAL WATER 2018 GENERAL RATE CASE UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report. Staff will attend the
  Public Participation Hearing and continue to update the City Council as new information
  becomes available.

  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reiterated the point he made previously that because
  Cal Water is an investor-owned organization and these improvements are infrastructure
  improvements, Cal Water should bear some of the burden of the project costs and there
  should be transparency in sharing the project costs and apportionment information.

  Mr. Armendariz briefly explained the CPUC rate setting process and the purpose of the
  Public Participation Hearing. Discussion ensued concerning the rate setting process and
  the costs that are being passed on to the ratepayers.

  Following discussion, the COUNCIL concurred to:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT AND DIRECT STAFF TO FURTHER
  ANALYZE CAL WATER’S RATE CASE UPDATE AND PREPARE A LETTER TO
  BE SUBMITTED TO THE CPUC AT THE PUBLIC PARTICIPATION HEARING
  ON BEHALF OF THE CITY FOR CITY COUNCIL REVIEW AT THE FEBRUARY
  12, 2019 COUNCIL MEETING.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION 21-18: APPLICANT EXER MORE THAN URGENT CARE;
  LOCATION 395 SILVER SPUR ROAD (PENINSULA SHOPPING CENTER-VESTAR)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) take public
  testimony; 3) discuss the issues; 4) close the Public Hearing; and 5) direct staff to prepare
  a resolution adopting Planning Application PA-21-18 approving the project.

  Planning Director David Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

  Scott Whitney, EXER More than Urgent Care, Vice President of Real Estate and
  Development addressed the City Council to provide information on the company’s foucs
  and purpose in the community and to furhter explain the way they provide medical service.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 22, 2019
   In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Whitney explained that the
  company’s prefernece is to be located in front facing, anchor locations rather than in the
  back of a of a retail center.

  Discussion ensued concernig the proposed location, parking, revenue generation and
  EXER’s expansion strategies.

  Jeff Axtell, Peninsula Center addresed the City Council in support of the project urging
  approal of the project. In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S inquiry, Mr.
  Axtel explained the potential revenue generation for this type of facility compared to a
  retail faciliy.

  MAYOR MITCHELL called for further public comment. Hearing none,

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING ON THIS MATTER.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBBER ZERUNYAN commented that he is not supportive of this use in
  this location and expressed concern regarding vehicle accessiblity and pedestiran traffic
  at this this location.

  MAYOR MITCHELL reviewed the options before the COUNCIL. Discussion ensued
  concerning the project and the pros and cons of this use in this particular location.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that she is generally supportive of this project
  given the difficulty the Peninsula Center has had in finding an occupant for this location.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he is generally supportive of this
  project given current policy and that this is not a prohibited use.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN and
  suggested that from a policy standpoint, the General Plan Advisory Committee is looking
  very closely at the commercial district.

  MAYOR MITCHELL also concurred.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION
  ADOPTING PLANNING APPLICATION PA-21-18 APPROVING THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Zerunyan

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 22, 2019
 B.  2019-20 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  THIS ITEM WAS NOT DISCUSSED. THE MATTER WAS CONTINUED TO
  ALLOW FOR PROPER NOTICING.

Recognizing that the individual to be recognized was now present, MAYOR MITCHELL
proceeded to take the Ceremonial Item.

CEREMONIAL ITEMS (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CERTIFICATE OF RECOGNITION FOR FIRE RESCUE

  MAYOR MITCHELL presented a Certificate of Recognition to Stuart Larking and Charlie
  Garabedian in recognition of their heroic efforts to help their neighbor in a desperate time
  of need when their home was ravaged by fire in the early hours of the morning.

NEW BUSINESS (CONTINUED)

A.  AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH SOUTHWEST PIPELINE FOR “YEAR 1” STORM
  DRAIN PIPE REHABILITATION PROJECT (taken out of order – see above)

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-19 – AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 16.04 OF THE ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SUBDIVISIONS AND REPEALING
  CHAPTERS 16.12, 16.16 AND 16.20 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) review the attached draft ordinance that
  would amend and restate Chapter 16.04 of the Rolling Hills Estates Municipal Code
  (RHEMC), pertaining to subdivisions; and repeal Chapters 16.12, 16.16 and 16.20 of the
  RHEMC; 2) introduce the attached ordinance for first reading; and 3) direct staff to bring
  back an ordinance for public hearing, second reading and adoption at the next City
  Council meeting of February 12, 2019.

  Planning Director David Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL INTRODUCE THE ORDINANCE FOR FIRST
  READING BY TITLE ONLY AND SCHEDULE A PUBLIC HEARING FOR
  SECOND READING OF THE ORDINANCE TO BE HELD ON TUESDAY,
  FEBRUARY 12, 2019 AT 7:30 P.M.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read the ordinance by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JANUARY 22, 2019
 C.  CAL WATER 2018 GENERAL RATE CASE UPDATE (taken out of order – see above)

D.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM:  CLEAN POWER
  ALLIANCE NON-RESIDENTIAL DEFAULT RATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council select a default rated of Lean Power (36%
  renewables) for non-residential customers; and that the City opt-up to 100% Green Power
  for municipal facilities.

  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN explained that

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE’S RECOMMENDATION TO SELECT A DEFAULT RATE OF LEAN
  POWER (36% RENEWABLES) FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL CUSTOMERS AND
  THAT THE CITY OPT-UP TO 100% GREEN POWER FOR MUNICIPAL
  FACILITIES.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

E.  2020 ELECTION DATE CHANGE

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to return with an ordinance changing
  the City’s election date to November of even years.

  City Clerk Heidi Luce provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Discussion ensued concerning the primary election date changes and the reason for
  those changes and the recent legislation that will put local candidates at the beginning of
  the ballot.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that he would support staff’s
  recommendation recognizing that there is no guarantee if the City moved the election to
  March that it would be possible that it would have to change again if the state changed
  the date of the primary. He stated that for continuity, November is the logical choice since
  it will not change and it aligns with the City’s Mayoral rotation.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that her concern is that moving back to
  November would extend terms again and would not be supportive of the democratic
  process. She further noted that staying with the Primary may provide more awareness for
  the local candidates.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JANUARY 22, 2019
   MAYOR MITCHELL noted that an advantage to moving to November is that it would then
  coincide with the City’s current Mayoral rotation. She concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR MITCHELL,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN WITH AN ORDINANCE
  CHANGING THE CITY’S ELECTION DATE TO NOVEMBER OF EVEN YEARS

  AYES:  Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Huff

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL, City Clerk Luce proided an overview of the County’s
  new voting experience which wiill be in place with the November 2020 election.

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO
  RENOVATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Park and Activities Commission’s
  recommendation to install a concrete pad and perimeter landscaping that include the
  planting of an Australian Peppermint Willow tree and Indian Hawthorne shrubs for the
  redesign of the City Hall Council Chamber patio.
